newsitem.title: USA: H&R Block names chief financial officer.
newsitem.headline: H&R Block names chief financial officer.

text.p: H&R Block Inc said Wednesday it named Ozzie Wenich, 54, as senior vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer.
He replaces George Robson, who resigned June 1. Wenich is currently president of H&R Block International and will retain that title.
Earlier, H&R Block reported net earnings of $47.8 million for fiscal 1997 ended April 30, down from year-ago earnings of $177.2 million.
H&R Block said its earnings were hurt by a $186.5 million pretax loss, which included $80.1 million in non-recurring charges and costs, reported by CompuServe Corp, of which it owns 80.1 percent.

Excluding CompuServe, Block's revenues grew nearly 26 percent to $1.1 billion from $871.5 million last year. Pretax earnings increased 14 percent to $225.1 million, while earnings per share increased more than 15 percent to $1.18 from $1.36.

Excluding a one-time gain realized on the MECA Software Inc sale and the write-down of certain impaired assets in fiscal 1996, pretax earnings rose 16.4 percent and earnings per share rose 17.2 percent.

"Clearly without CompuServe's results, H&R Block exceeded its goals to grow revenues and earnings by 15 percent," Frank Salizzoni, president, said in a statement. "H&R Block Tax Services, H&R Block International and Block Financial all contributed to these strong results."
